_comment: ADR-0016 D2: cost is computed from per-thread USAGE (Claude-Platform-sourced,
GET /v1/sessions/{id}/threads) times this git-pinned, model-aware,
cache-bucket-aware price table -- there is NO public per-token price-list API
(confirmed live 2026-07-07: GET /v1/models carries capabilities/max_tokens/effort
but no pricing field at all), so prices must be pinned somewhere. Anti-drift is
handled by (a) isolating every price in this ONE small, reviewed file, each tier
carrying its own effective_from/effective_until, and (b) `harness/cost.py`'s
`--check-pricing-drift` guard, which fails loud when today's date falls outside
every tier's window for a model family.
SCHEMA (three layers, smallest-to-most-specific -- see harness/cost.py's
`resolve_price_tier()`):
1. the top-level `cache_multipliers` block = the DEFAULT cache ratios, each
relative to the applicable rate card's OWN base input rate (a cache-write
token costs `write_5m`/`write_1h` x that input rate; a cache-read token
costs `read` x it);
2. an OPTIONAL per-model `cache_multipliers` object, MERGED OVER those
defaults key-by-key (so `{"read": 0.05}` overrides only the read ratio and
inherits the 1.25/2.0 write ratios);
3. an OPTIONAL per-tier `long_prompt` object -- a SECOND rate card for models
Anthropic prices by prompt length, with its own input/output rates and its
own `threshold_prompt_tokens`. The cache multipliers (own or inherited)
apply to whichever card a request lands on, against THAT card's input rate.
The pre-2026-10-11 version of this file asserted the cache ratios applied
UNIFORMLY across every family. That is NO LONGER TRUE (layer 2 above exists
precisely because it stopped being true), and no new model may be added here on
the assumption that it is -- read the pricing page's own per-model cache rates.
Output rates are still pinned explicitly per tier, never formula-derived from
the input rate (ADR-0016 D2: 'prices must be pinned, not formula-derived').
CAPTURED 2026-10-11 (verified against the live pricing page the same day, for
the Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 matched eval):
- `claude-opus-5-5` $4/$20 per MTok, 5m write $5, 1h write $8, cache read
$0.20 = 0.05x base input -- the page's own footnote: 'Cache hits and
refreshes on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are priced at 0.05x the
base input price.' Hence the per-model `cache_multipliers: {read: 0.05}`
override; the write ratios are the usual 1.25x/2x.
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` $2/$10, 5m write $2.50, 1h write $4, cache read $0.10
= the same 0.05x read override.
- `claude-haiku-5-5` has TWO rate cards, chosen PER REQUEST by prompt length:
Both cards' cache rates are exactly the DEFAULT 1.25/2.0/0.1 ratios of that
card's own input rate, so Haiku 5.5 needs NO cache override -- only the
`long_prompt` card. Page wording: 'A request's prompt length counts all of
its input tokens, including cache reads and cache writes. Each request is
priced on its own: a request over the threshold pays the higher prices even
when part of its prompt is a cache hit, and earlier requests keep the prices
they were billed at.' This is why a rate-carded model CANNOT be priced from
a thread's aggregate usage -- `harness/cost.py` prices it per REQUEST from
the session events' `span.model_request_end.model_usage`, with a fail-loud
integrity check against the thread's own totals.
- `claude-sonnet-5` CORRECTED: this table previously carried a 'standard from
2026-09-01' tier at $3/$15, transcribed from the then-scheduled increase.
The page's own footnote now reads: the $2/$10 introductory pricing 'is now
the standard price. The previously scheduled increase to $3/$15 ... on
September 1, 2026 will not occur.' So Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 on EVERY date, one
tier, cache read unchanged at 0.1x = $0.20. (Tier history, kept honest: the
$2/$10 rate was introduced as 'introductory' with an effective_until of
2026-08-31; nothing re-priced on 2026-09-01, and no run was ever costed
against the phantom $3/$15 tier -- every committed run record predates it
and re-prices identically under this correction.)
- `claude-haiku-4-5` ($1/$5) and `claude-opus-4-8` ($5/$25) are UNCHANGED and
deliberately retained: the production config ran on Haiku 4.5, and every
eval run committed before 2026-10-11 was judged by Opus 4.8 -- both must
keep re-pricing to exactly their recorded numbers.
Judge model (owner-directed 2026-10-11, docs/adr/0016 amendment): ALL FOUR
judges now run on `claude-opus-5-5` (previously Opus 4.8) -- so judge-cost
pricing picks up that 0.05x cache-read rate, which matters a lot for the
web-tool judges whose server-side loop re-reads a cached prefix every
iteration. Note the pricing page's own tokenizer caveat: Opus 4.7+ (incl. 4.8,
Opus 5, Opus 5.5) and Sonnet 5/5.5 use a newer tokenizer that produces ~30%
MORE tokens for the same text than Haiku 4.5's tokenizer -- not a pricing.json
concern, but worth knowing when reading a judge-cost.json total or comparing a
Haiku 4.5 candidate's token counts against a Haiku 5.5 one.
The 'web_search' block below is a SEPARATE, flat, per-call (not per-token, not
per-model) rate Anthropic bills web-search tool invocations at -- confirmed live
2026-07-07 against the web-search-tool docs page ('$10 per 1,000 searches' =
$0.01/search) and UNCHANGED at the 2026-10-11 capture; web fetch is NOT priced
here because it is billed at token cost only, no separate per-call fee.

claude-sonnet-5._comment: Tier history: the $2/$10 rate shipped as 'introductory' with a scheduled increase to $3/$15 on 2026-09-01. Per the pricing page's 2026-10-11 footnote that increase WILL NOT OCCUR and $2/$10 is now the standard price -- one tier, every date.

claude-haiku-5-5._comment: TWO rate cards, chosen per REQUEST by prompt length (input + cache reads + cache writes). A thread's aggregate usage cannot pick a card, so harness/cost.py prices this family per request from the session events.
